469.n: accent from enclitic ῥα; ὅτε δή 'when at last'
epic ἔην = ἦν: 'a year was past', as τρίτον ἐστὶν ἔτος 2.89 (Merry on 10.469)
in tmesis: περὶ … ἔτραπον, intransitive second aorist, 'returned on their course' to begin a new year, as περιπλομένων ἐνιαυτῶν 1.16 (Merry on 10.469)

470.n: genitive absolute with φθινόντων; the line, wanting in the best manuscripts and in Eustathius, has been rejected since Wolf (Murray prints it), and is probably borrowed from Hesiod, Theogony 59 (Merry on 10.470 and his critical note)

470.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. pl. masc.

470.n: in tmesis with τελέσθη (περιτελέω 'complete the round')
neuter plural subject with singular verb
the long days of spring, as 18.367 (Merry on 10.470)
unaugmented (= ἐτελέσθη); in tmesis with περί: 'came full circle'

471.n: καὶ τότε 'then', in the apodosis of ὅτε δή (469)

471.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

471.n: plural as if from a 3rd-decl. ἐρίηρ

472.n: = δαιμόνιε; implies a man under some superhuman influence, whose conduct excites wonder (Merry on 10.472); as Iliad 2.190
uncontracted -εο (= μιμνήσκου); middle 'remember, think of', + gen.

473.n: 'spoken by a god, decreed' (θεός + φημί), + inf.; second accent from enclitic ἐστι
+ acc. οἶκον (474); καὶ ἱκέσθαι / οἶκον ἐς ὑψόροφον as 7.76–77

474.n: the line = 7.77 (as 5.42, with σήν for ἑήν); Merry prints οἶκον ἐυκτίμενον, as 6.315

475.n: the line as 406; 475–479 are wanting in three manuscripts and in Eustathius, and Wolf and most editors after him reject them (Merry's critical note on 10.475)

476.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
476.n: root aorist κατέδυν: 'until the setting of the sun'

477.n: imperfect, the same in form as the present; the line = 468, 9.162

477.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

479.n: plural of the rooms of one house; μέγαρα σκιόεντα as 1.365

480.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
480.n: root aorist; + gen. 'mount, go up on to'; Κίρκης ἐπέβην περικαλλέος εὐνῆς 347

481.n: epic γούνων (= γονάτων); genitive of what one entreats by, as λίσσομαι Ζηνός 2.68 (Merry on 10.481)
augmented with the λ doubled (= ἐλιτάνευσα), as ἐλλιτάνευε Iliad 22.414

482.n: accent from enclitic μιν; the line = 4.550; wanting in three manuscripts and in Eustathius, it has generally been rejected since Bekker (Merry's critical note on 10.482)

482.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

482.n: 'winged': words that fly to the listener

no such promise is told; Merry supposes it given in her oath (345), in her welcome (460), or in the unrecorded year (Merry on 10.483)

484.n: οἶκος with the suffix -δε 'toward', printed as one word
epic future infinitive -έμεναι (= πέμψειν), explaining ὑπόσχεσιν (483)
dative of the person, standing by the verb like an ethic dative, while ἑτάρων (485) goes with θυμός (Merry on 10.484)
perfect passive of σεύω with present sense: 'is set in motion, is eager'

485.n: genitive with θυμός (484) after the dative μοι, a change of case as 9.256–257 (Merry on 10.484)

486.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

486.n: with the subjunctive without κε, a rare use (Merry on 10.486)

489.n: μίμνω = μένω; plural, to Odysseus and his men

490.n: + inf.; the subject (ὑμᾶς) understood, taken up by χρησομένους (492)
adverbial: 'first', before the voyage home; Merry compares Virgil, Aeneid 3.384–386 (Merry on 10.490)

491.n: 'dread, awful', in Homer only of Persephone as Hades' consort (Iliad 9.457, 9.569; again 534, 564); Merry rejects 'praiseworthy' (as if from ἔπαινος) and derives it from ἐπί + αἰνός 'dread', or would write with Buttmann καὶ ἐπʼ αἰνή (Merry on 10.491)

492.n: dative with χρησομένους; the line again 565

492.p: verb · fut. part. mid. acc. pl. masc.
492.n: future participle of purpose; middle χράομαι 'consult (an oracle)', + dat., as 8.81; accusative, agreeing with the subject of τελέσαι καὶ ἱκέσθαι (490)
'of Thebes' (the word is a man's name at Iliad 8.120); Teiresias belongs to the Theban cycle of legend (Merry on 10.492)
epic gen. -αο; the Theban seer, to whom, in later stories, Zeus gave prophecy and long life in amends for his blindness (Merry on 10.492)

493.n: Ionic gen. -ηος, as πόληος 1.185, in apposition to Τειρεσίαο; the reading of one Venice manuscript, followed by most editors, the others μάντιος (Merry's critical note on 10.493)
a special privilege among the dead, who keep no φρένες, as the shade of Patroclus (Iliad 23.103–104) (Merry on 10.495)
two-termination adjective: -οι with feminine φρένες; second accent from enclitic εἰσι

494.n: 'to whom even after his death' (Merry on 10.494)

494.p: verb · pf. part. act. dat. sg. masc.
494.n: epic perfect participle τεθνηώς (= τεθνηκώς): 'though dead'
unaugmented aorist (= ἔπορε); no present attested
queen of the dead, wife of Hades

495.n: drawn into the dative of τῷ (494) from the usual accusative with the infinitive (Merry on 10.495)
perfect with present sense 'be wise' (participle πεπνυμένος); Cicero renders 'solum sapere, ceteros umbrarum vagari modo' (Merry on 10.495)
epic τοί = οἱ; Plato, quoting the line, reads ταὶ δέ (Merry's critical note on 10.495)
Ionic σκιή = σκιά, in predicate: the dead are not invisible but without substance; Plato faults the line (Republic 386d) (Merry on 10.495)

496.n: 'was broken down' (κλάω 'break'); κατεκλάσθη φίλον ἦτορ in Homer only in the Odyssey (4.481, 4.538, 9.256, 198, 566, 12.277)

497.n: unaugmented (= ἔκλαιον); 497–499 as 4.539–541, there ἐν ψαμάθοισι 'on the sand'
epic dat. pl. -εσσι; plural for one bed

497.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

497.n: κῆρ 'heart', not κήρ 'doom'; Merry prints οὐδέ τι θυμός

498.n: epic ζώω = ζάω; ζώειν καὶ ὁρᾶν φάος ἠελίοιο as Iliad 24.558

499.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
499.n: the participles go with ἐκορέσθην: 'had my fill of weeping and rolling'

499.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
499.n: middle 'roll oneself', a sign of grief, as 4.541
aorist passive: 'had my fill of', + participle (unaugmented κορέσθην at 4.541)

500.n: καὶ τότε δή 'then at last', in the apodosis of ἐπεί (499)

500.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

500.n: epic ἔειπον (= εἶπον); the line as 5.96, in the first person

501.n: accusative of the way with ἡγεμονεύσει
'lead, guide', + acc. of the way, as 6.261

502.n: εἰς Ἄϊδος (δόμον) 'to the house of Hades'; Merry rejects the reading Ἄϊδόσδʼ (Fäsi), since Ἀΐδης is in Homer always a person, not a place, and a question with γάρ is usually followed by δέ or ἀλλά (Merry's critical note on 10.502)
gen. of the by-form Ἄϊς: '(the house) of Hades'
enclitic, accented before enclitic τις; οὔ πώ τις 'no one ever yet'

505.n: adverbial 'at all'; accented before enclitic τοι
epic τοι = σοι; dative with μελέσθω
best taken with μελέσθω, as though he might hang about the ship waiting for a pilot (Merry on 10.505)
middle μέλομαι 'be a care to', + dat.; the form only here in Homer

506.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
506.n: transitive aorist ἔστησα 'set up'; the participles go with ἧσθαι (507)
in tmesis with πετάσσας (ἀναπετάννυμι 'spread out'); acute before enclitic θʼ

506.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
506.n: epic -σσ- (= πετάσας); in tmesis with ἀνά, as 4.783, 8.54

507.n: infinitive for imperative: sit still while the wind does the work
with the subjunctive: 'will carry', as if that were the North Wind's intent (Merry on 10.507); accent from enclitic τοι

508.n: epic gen. -οιο; for Homer a river with a current, ringing the earth and distinct from the sea, which a ship could cross to the shore beyond (Merry on 10.508)

509.n: as 9.116, to which Merry refers (Merry on 10.509); the scholia reject ἐλάχεια 'very small', unfit for the precinct of Persephone (Merry's critical note on 10.509)

510.n: Ionic ἰτέη = ἰτέα 'willow'; in Homer only here and Iliad 21.350; the word had an initial digamma (Merry on 10.510)

'losing their fruit' (ὄλλυμι + καρπός): Pliny (Natural History 16.26) explains that the willow sheds its seed before it ripens; a fit tree for the groves of the dead, as the scholia say (Merry on 10.510); in Homer only here

511.n: 'there, on the spot', explained by ἐπʼ Ὠκεανῷ (Merry on 10.511)
'run ashore'; infinitive for imperative, the apodosis of ὁπότʼ ἄν (508) (Merry on 10.511)

512.n: Ionic gen. -εω, one syllable by synizesis
elsewhere beneath the earth (Iliad 22.482); in this voyage Odysseus stays on the earth's surface, at the far edge of the world (Merry on 10.512)

513.n: 'at the entrance to the house of Hades' (Merry on 10.513)

in Homer only here; Pausanias thought the scene drawn from the Acherusian lake in Thesprotia with its rivers Acheron and Cocytus, but the rivers may rather have taken their names from the poetry (Merry on 10.513)
'blazing with fire' (πῦρ + φλεγέθω); in Homer only here; Merry takes these rivers for a later invention than the Styx (Merry on 10.513)
plural verb between two singular subjects, the figure the grammarians called σχῆμα Ἀλκμανικόν (Merry on 10.513)

514.n: 'the river of wailing' (κωκυτός 'wailing', Iliad 22.409); printed Κώκυτος, with a second accent from enclitic θʼ; in Homer only here
the river by which the gods swear; how the Cocytus can be a branch of the Styx is not easy to see (Merry on 10.515)
'broken off' (cf. ἀπορρήγνυμι), used as a noun: a branch stream; Στυγὸς ὕδατός ἐστιν ἀπορρώξ as Iliad 2.755, of the Titaresius

515.n: Ionic πέτρη = πέτρα; a loose construction, 'there is a rock and a confluence': perhaps a ledge over which the joined streams plunge into the Acheron (Merry on 10.515)
'a coming together, confluence' (ξυνίημι = συνίημι), in its literal sense; in Homer only here; second accent from enclitic τε
epic δύω = δύο, indeclinable, with the genitive ποταμῶν
'loud-resounding' (ἐρι- 'very' + δοῦπος 'thud, din'): the noise of a cataract (Merry on 10.515)

516.n: = ἔπειτα (τ aspirated before the rough breathing of ἥρως)
vocative, same form as the nominative

517.n: the pit used in place of an altar in the cult of the gods below (Merry on 10.517)

'a cubit long' (πυγών, the forearm from elbow to knuckles); in Homer only here and 11.25
ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα 'this way and that', in length and breadth (Merry on 10.517)

518.n: 'libation' (χέω), the proper term for a drink offering to the dead (Merry on 10.518); in Homer only here and 11.26
contracted (= χέεσθαι); infinitive for imperative; χοὴν χεῖσθαι, cognate accusative

519.n: adverbial neuter plural; the line again 11.27
'honey-mixture' (μέλι + κεράννυμι), honey mixed with milk (Merry on 10.519); instrumental dative; in Homer only here and 11.27

520.n: = αὖτε, τ → θ before rough breathing: 'again, next'

in tmesis: ἐπὶ … παλύνειν; infinitive for imperative

'without strength' (ἀ- + μένος), as Merry takes it, against Döderlein's 'fleeting' (ἀ- + μένω); of a wounded man Iliad 5.887 (Merry on 10.521); ἀμενηνὰ κάρηνα again 536
'heads', for the persons of the dead

522.n: the line gives the words of the vow implied in γουνοῦσθαι (Merry on 10.522); 522–524 again 11.30–32
'barren', fit for the dead, who are themselves barren (scholia, in Merry on 10.522); not στεῖρα 'keel' (Iliad 1.482)

523.n: future infinitive of the vow, after γουνοῦσθαι (521)
used as a noun: 'costly things', such as honey, flowers, garments and arms, as Eustathius lists them (Merry on 10.523)

524.n: = ἀπάνευθε with movable ν: at a separate spot, so that his offering is not confused with that to the rest of the dead (Merry on 10.524)

525.n: = παμμέλανα (πᾶς + μέλας); black victims for the gods below, white for the gods above (Merry on 10.525); in Homer again 3.6, 11.33
epic dat. pl. -οισι; dative with μεταπρέπει
epic dat. pl. -οισιν; plural: 'yours', of Odysseus' house

aorist subjunctive (= λίσηαι), aorist ἐλισάμην with a single σ
more than a stock epithet: many of those about to appear are heroes and famous women (Merry on 10.526)

529.n: middle ἵεμαι 'press on, make for', + gen.: 'moving towards the current of the (Ocean-)stream', so turning back to face the living world, explaining ἀπονόσφι (528) (Merry on 10.529)
epic gen. -οιο: the stream of Oceanus

from epic ἕταρος; dat. pl. -οισι(ν), with ἐποτρῦναι
aorist infinitive as if from ἀνώγω (built on the perfect ἄνωγα): 'command'; not ἀνοίγω 'open'

532.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. pl. neut.
532.n: perfect passive participle: 'with their throats cut'

533.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. pl. masc.
533.n: referring to ἑτάροισιν (531) but drawn into the accusative by the infinitive (Merry on 10.532); 533–534 again 11.46–47

535.n: ξίφος ὀξὺ ἐρυσσάμενος παρὰ μηροῦ as 126, 294, 9.300 (ἄορ ὀξύ 321)

535.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
535.n: epic -σσ- in the aorist; middle 'draw (one's own)'

537.n: genitive with ἆσσον; the line again 11.50, 11.89
epic gen. -αο; genitive of the person asked, with πυθέσθαι

539.n: with the subjunctive: what will happen; accent from enclitic τοι
the stages and distances of the voyage

542.n: in tmesis with ἕσσεν (ἀμφιέννυμι 'put clothes about'), as 4.253
second accent from enclitic τε; χλαῖνάν τε χιτῶνά τε as 5.229, where Odysseus dresses himself
in apposition to χλαῖνάν τε χιτῶνά τε: 'for clothing' (Merry on 10.542)
in tmesis: ἀμφὶ … ἕσσεν; epic aorist ἕσσα of ἕννυμι 'clothe', with two accusatives

543.n: a large cloth worn as a cloak

544.n: = βάλετο, unaugmented; in tmesis with περί (= περιεβάλετο); middle 'put around oneself'

545.n: the line as 5.232, where Aristarchus read ἐφύπερθε for ἐπέθηκε (Merry's critical note on 10.545)
a veil that could be let fall over the face, as 5.232

546.n: he slept, it seems, in the inner chamber and his men in the colonnades, so that he passes the length of the house (Merry on 10.546)

546.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

547.n: ἄνδρα ἕκαστον, in apposition to ἑταίρους (546)

548.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

548.n: 'sleep soundly', with ὕπνον as Iliad 10.159; Merry connects it with ἄημι 'breathe', 'breathing sleep's deep breath', against the scholia's 'culling sleep' as from ἄωτος 'flower' (Merry on 10.548)

550.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); dative of the person: 'their spirit'

551.n: οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδέ = ἀλλʼ οὐ μὴν οὐδέ: 'but not even thence could I carry off my comrades unharmed' (Merry on 10.551)

552.n: the youngest of the companions; his shade is the first Odysseus meets in the underworld (11.51)

553.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
553.n: intransitive perfect ἄρηρα 'be fitted, firm': 'steady in mind', like the later φρενήρης (Merry on 10.553)

555.n: 'coolness' (ψύχω 'breathe, cool'); uncontracted gen. -εος; genitive with ἱμείρων; in Homer only here

555.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

555.n: aorist middle of καταλέγω 'lay down': 'lay down to sleep', as Iliad 9.690; on the flat roof, open to the air (Eustathius, in Merry on 10.558)

555.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

556.p: verb · pres. part. mid. gen. pl. masc.

556.n: a heavy, thudding sound: their tread

556.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

557.n: 2nd aorist middle ἐκλαθόμην 'forget utterly', + inf. καταβῆναι (558)

558.n: adverbial: 'back again', after he had climbed to the roof (Merry on 10.558); the line again 11.63
root aorist κατέβην; infinitive with ἐκλάθετο (557)

558.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
558.n: the important clause: the ladder was the only safe way down from the flat roof (Merry on 10.558)

559.n: 'straight down' (κατά + ἀντικρύ), + gen. τέγεος; in Homer only here and 11.64
in tmesis with ἐάγη (560) (ἐξάγνυμι 'break out of'), as ἐξ αὐχένʼ ἔαξε Iliad 11.175 (Merry on 10.560)

560.n: genitive of separation with ἐκ … ἐάγη: 'wrenched out of its vertebrae' (Merry on 10.560); as Iliad 14.466
in tmesis with ἐκ (559); 2nd aorist passive ἐάγην of ἄγνυμι (from ϝάγνυμι); the line again 11.65
Ἄϊδος (gen. of Ἄϊς = Ἀΐδης: '(the house) of Hades') with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word, as 3.410

561.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. pl. masc.

561.n: placed after its noun τοῖσιν, as Iliad 24.777

562.n: middle with active sense: 'think, suppose', as 6.200; 'Ye deem, I trow' (Merry on 10.562)
οἶκον with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word; οἶκόνδε φίλην ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν as 5.204

563.n: epic ἧμιν = ἡμῖν; taken up by the accusative χρησομένους (565), as δείραντας after ἑτάροισιν (531–533) (Merry on 10.563)

565.p: verb · fut. part. mid. acc. pl. masc.
565.n: future participle of purpose (χράομαι 'consult'), as 492; accusative after the dative ἧμιν (563) (Merry on 10.532, 10.563)

566.n: singular of the heart of each

567.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
567.n: in tmesis: ἑζόμενοι … κατʼ (καθέζομαι 'sit down'), as Iliad 13.653
= κατά; in tmesis with ἑζόμενοι; κατʼ αὖθι is La Roche's text, with a scholion in the Iliad, for the common καταῦθι (Merry's critical note on 10.567)
unaugmented imperfect, as from a by-form γόω (γόον Iliad 6.500); not the noun γόων
middle 'tear (one's own)'; unaugmented; second accent from enclitic τε

568.n: = ἀλλά; the line = 202; ἀλλʼ οὐ γάρ 'but (it was in vain), for …'
Ionic πρῆξις = πρᾶξις 'getting done, gain', as Iliad 24.524

568.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. pl. masc.

569.n: ἐπὶ νῆα θοὴν καὶ θῖνα θαλάσσης as 402, 407

570.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

571.n: the apodosis of ὅτε δή (569) begins here (Merry on 10.573)

571.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.

572.n: with ὄιν: 'a ram (sheep)', the victims of 527, tethered ready for the sacrifice (Merry on 10.573)
epic ὄϊς (Attic οἶς); with ἀρνειόν and with θῆλυν understood, as 527
the form in -υς serving as feminine, as 527; second accent from enclitic τε

573.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
573.n: 'having easily slipped past us': the manner of her going (Merry on 10.573)

573.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

574.n: = ἴδοιτο; middle aorist 'see'; potential optative with ἄν (573)
= ἔνθα; ἢ ἔνθʼ ἢ ἔνθα 'backward or forward, to and fro', at any time or place: the gods are seen or unseen at will (Merry on 10.574)

574.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
